subject: Uptime discrepancy & maintenance window reconciliation for Nimbus order form
messages:
From: Ethan Ross <ethan@nicetech.co>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@nimbus.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observed uptime numbers vs. Order Form SLA (account: Nimbus)

Sean —

We've been compiling our uptime metrics for November and there appears to be a delta between what Nimbus is seeing and the uptime measurement defined in the order form (section 2.1). We're seeing ~98.3% aggregated availability for the EU region during a two-week maintenance period that Redwood categorized as 'rolling maintenance' — the credit math in your current SLA doesn't seem to align with our monitoring.

Can you help reconcile: (1) the measurement window used for credits, (2) how rolling maintenance windows are excluded, and (3) what evidence you need to validate/trigger a service credit? I've attached the logs we captured (nimbus_uptime_logs_202611.csv).

We'd like to avoid opening a formal dispute if this can be handled in-line, but procurement is asking for clarity before we sign v3 of the order form.

Thanks,
Ethan Ross
Procurement Manager — Nimbus Inc
attachments: nimbus_uptime_logs_202611.csv (csv)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan@nicetech.co>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed uptime numbers vs. Order Form SLA (account: Nimbus)

Hi Ethan —

Thanks for the data and the heads-up. I'm looking into this and looping in Lauren (legal) and Kim (sales ops). Quick answers up front:

- Credit measurement window: credits are calculated monthly, using our service-side P95 availability for the customer's provisioned region, with exclusions for pre-scheduled maintenance if notified 72+ hours in advance.
- Rolling maintenance: by default we treat rolling maintenance as included in the maintenance bucket if it meets the pre-notice/slot criteria; otherwise it counts toward availability.
- Evidence: we generally need (a) the customer's monitoring snapshot, (b) our infra logs, and (c) a short timeline to validate.

Can Lauren confirm whether the maintenance carveout language in the draft order form v3 matches what you're seeing? Kim — can you pull the internal incident logs for the EU region 2026-11-15..2026-11-28 and attach?

I'll propose we calendar a 30-min reconciliation call this week.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: sean@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed uptime numbers vs. Order Form SLA (account: Nimbus)

Sean / Kim —

I've reviewed the latest orderform redlines (redlines_sla_orderform_v3.pdf). A few legal notes that matter for negotiation:

1) "Scheduled Maintenance" definition — current draft says: "scheduled maintenance means pre-published maintenance windows notified >=72 hours in advance." That is workable, but we need to (a) include a timezone normalization clause (SLA uses customer's contract region time) and (b) clarify "rolling maintenance" as a multi-site staggered activity that may overlap with measured windows.

2) Measurement methodology — we prefer to keep Redwood's internal monitoring as the single source of truth for credit triggers, but accept cross-evidence. Suggest language: "Customer monitoring may be provided as corroborating evidence but does not override Redwood metrics unless mutually agreed."

3) Credit cap & pro-rata treatment — legal wants the credit ladder simplified for procurement (three bands rather than four). See suggested text in the attached PDF.

Marissa — please confirm whether the simplified ladder aligns with the standard commercial playbook.

I'll join the call if needed.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: sean@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Ethan Ross <ethan@nicetech.co>, contracts@nimbus.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed uptime numbers vs. Order Form SLA (account: Nimbus)

Sean / all —

Attached: internal incident summary and infra timeline for EU region (2026-11-15..2026-11-28). Key points:

- We had two rolling maintenance events (11/17 and 11/24). Both were scheduled with customer-impact windows of ~45 minutes across staggered shards; notices went to customers 80+ hours in advance, but the published maintenance notice used PST timestamps — we'll add timezone normalization per Lauren's note.
- There was one short degradation on 11/21 between 02:13-02:35 UTC due to a misrouted batch job; our control plane shows a brief P95 dip consistent with ~0.4% availability impact for that day.

Attachments: redwood_eu_incident_202611.pdf; redlines_sla_orderform_v3.pdf; proposed_maintenance_calendar.ics

Action items: Sean to propose call times; Legal to confirm language; Sales ops to produce reconciled credit math.

Thanks —
Kim

Thanks for the quick replies and the docs. A couple of clarifying items from Nimbus procurement/security:

- Timezone normalization: procurement wants all maintenance notices to be normalized to the customer's billing region. Otherwise we risk mismatched expectations.
- Evidence threshold: procurement is asking for an "evidence packet" format so they can handle credit requests without legal each time — ideally a 1-pager with timestamps, Redwood metric snippets, and the customer's supplied logs.

We're available for a call on Friday (12/4) morning PST. If you can send the evidence packet template ahead of time that would be helpful.

Ethan

Ethan / team —

Thanks again — quick recap and next steps so procurement can proceed: 

1) Evidence packet: Kim attached a lightweight template (one-pager) to the Drive link; I'll extract and attach a copy to the DocuSign package. That template will include: customer log excerpts, Redwood P95/uptime graphs, incident timeline, and suggested credit calculation.
2) Maintenance timezone clause: Legal (Lauren) will propose tightened wording that normalizes published times to the customer's contract region and includes explicit notice window semantics.
3) Credit ladder: Marissa confirmed we can offer a three-band credit ladder for this order (1%–3%, 3%–6%, >6%) consistent with our commercial exceptions.
4) Meeting: we'll keep Friday's slot tentative but I've asked sales ops to produce the reconciled math by EOD Friday so procurement can finish internal sign-off.

I'll upload the reconciled calc and the evidence packet template to the Drive folder and ping when DocuSign is ready.
